report:
Contrary to your assumption, medical evidence demonstrates that the health claim is **true**: bystander hands-only (chest compression-only) CPR significantly increases survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest compared to receiving no bystander CPR.

### Key Evidence

1. **Substantially Higher Survival**: Data from the American Heart Association and observational registries indicate that immediate bystander CPR—including hands-only CPR—doubles or triples a patient's chance of survival compared to no intervention (https://cpr.heart.org/en/resources/cpr-facts-and-stats, https://zipdo.co/hands-only-cpr-statistics/).
2. **Population-Level Proof**: A nationwide study evaluating 18 years of out-of-hospital cardiac arrests found that 30-day survival doubled for patients receiving compression-only CPR compared to those receiving no CPR (https://medicalxpress.com/news/2019-04-compression-only-cpr-survival-out-of-hospital-cardiac.html).
3. **Potential Sources of Confusion**: Scepticism often stems from comparisons between CPR types rather than CPR versus no CPR. While conventional CPR (compressions with rescue breathing) can be superior in pediatric cases or asphyxial arrests (https://www.resuscitationjournal.com/article/S0300-9572(18)31067-0/fulltext), hands-only CPR remains vastly superior to providing no assistance at all.

### Conclusion

Maintaining continuous blood flow through chest compressions preserves vital organ function until emergency medical services arrive. Major health organizations strongly recommend hands-only CPR because doing chest compressions alone provides a major survival benefit over doing nothing.
